{{Short description|Iranian mathematician}}
'''Abū al-Jūd Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. al-Layth''' {{Langx|fa|ابو جود محمد بن احمد بن لیث}} was an [[Iranian peoples|Iranian]] mathematician who lived during 10th century and was a contemporary of [[al-Biruni]]. He used [[conic]]s to solve [[Quartic function|quartic]] and cubic equations, a century before the more famous work of [[Omar Khayyam]],<ref>{{Cite book| publisher = Springer Science & Business Media| isbn = 978-3-642-36736-6| last1 = Sidoli| first1 = Nathan| last2 = Brummelen| first2 = Glen Van| title = From Alexandria, Through Baghdad: Surveys and Studies in the Ancient Greek and Medieval Islamic Mathematical Sciences in Honor of J.L. Berggren| date = 2013-10-30|page=110}}</ref> although his solution did not deal with all the cases.<ref>{{Cite book| publisher = Springer Science & Business Media| isbn = 978-3-642-51599-6| last = Waerden| first = Bartel L. van der| title = A History of Algebra: From al-Khwārizmī to Emmy Noether| date = 2013-06-29|page=29}}</ref>

== Life ==

Not much is known about his life. He seems to have lived in the east of [[Khurasan]], within [[Samanid Empire|Samanid]] territory.  [[Sa'id al-Andalusi]] claimed that he lived in Valencia (Balansiya) and died in 1014 or 1015, but other sources didn't mention these information. It is likely that he became a scribe after acquiring basic knowledge on mathematics.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia|last1=Ali|first1=Mowlavi, Muhammad|last2=Rahim|first2=Gholami|title=Abū al-Jūd|encyclopedia=Encyclopaedia Islamica|language=en|doi=10.1163/1875-9831_isla_com_0092}}</ref>
